docs.title: Welcome to Tomiio's Blog
docs.text:
Hello and thanks for visiting my blog! Here, I share my experiences, projects, and insights on topics like embedded systems, robotics, programming, and more. Whether you're a fellow developer, hobbyist, or just curious, I hope you'll find something interesting and useful.

This blog is my way of sharing stories from my journey—documenting the challenges, discoveries, and lessons learned through my projects.

Check out my projects at: - 11/2022 - Autonomous Driving Vehicle. - 07/2023 - BLDC Driver (FOC - Field Oriented Control). - 10/2023 - Handsignator (Deaf-mute disablities support device). - 10/2025 - Autonomous Wheelchair

docs.title: 1. Introduction
docs.text: Welcome to the documentation of my Autonomous Driving Vehicle project developed for the Bosch Future Mobility Challenge (BFMC). This project is a 1:10 scale autonomous car platform designed to perform real-world driving tasks such as traffic signs perception, lane keeping, obstacle avoidance, intersection handling, and autonomous parking.

docs.title: 2. Objectives
docs.text:
• Compete in the BFMC competition.
  • Develop a robust autonomous driving stack combining perception, planning, and control based on Sensors (Camera, Distance Sensor) and Actuators (BLDC Motor and Servo).
  • Integrate embedded hardware (STM32F401RE Nucleo, Jetson Xavier NX) with ROS.
  • Demonstrate safe and reliable driving behavior in a constrained track environment.
  • The vehicle should be able to perform the challenges:
    • Lane keeping
    • Follow the traffic rules detected from traffic signs
    • Obstacle avoidance (Pedestrians and Other Vehicles on road)
    • Intersection handling
    • Autonomous parking
    • Complete the planned path by localization and navigation

docs.title: 3.1 Computing Units
docs.text:
• NVIDIA Jetson Xavier NX
    • Runs Ubuntu + ROS
    • Handle sensor input (fusion), AI inference, perception and decision making (motion planning and control command)
  • STM32F401RE
    • Runs Mbed OS
    • Handles low-level motor and steering control (from received control command)
    • Interfaces with sensors (IMU, encoder, ultrasonic) and input to the Single Board Computer (Jetson Xavier NX)

docs.title: 3.2 Sensors
docs.text: Sensor Purpose Camera (Logitech C922) Lane detection, sign detection IMU Vehicle orientation and angular velocity Encoder Wheel angular velocity estimation V2X Position estimation Ultrasonic sensor Obstacle distance

docs.title: 3.3 Actuators
docs.text:
• BLDC motor + ESC (longitudinal control)
  • Servo motor (steering, Ackermann geometry)

docs.title: 4. System Architecture
docs.text:
The system is divided into the following modules:

4.1. Perception

  • Lane detection (camera-based, DBSCANS).
  • Obstacle detection (ultrasonic sensors and Yolov8 Object detection).
  • Signs & traffic light recognition (Yolov8 Object detection).

4.2. Planning

  • Behavior planner (FSM-based).
  • Global/local path generation (Dijkstra search for global path and static path for local path).
  • Obstacle avoidance & lane switching.

4.3. Actuator Control

  • Low-level motor + steering control (PID & Stanley).
  • Safety overrides & emergency stop (Cruise control).

docs.title: 5.2 ROS Topics
docs.text: Topic Description /image_raw Camera raw image /lanePerception Lane parameters output from Lane detection model /trafficSigns Object parameters output from Object detection model /ultraSonic Ultrasonic distance detection data /imu IMU data /encoder Encoder data /gps GPS data /position Position estimation data /job Behavior command /command Speed & steering command

docs.title: 6.1 Overview
docs.text: The Perception module provides real-time environmental understanding for the autonomous vehicle. Its primary functions include lane detection, object and traffic sign recognition, traffic light state estimation, and intersection detection. The output of this module supplies structured information to the planning and control layers through ROS topics.
